newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay share index tumbles 2.43 pct, nervous trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay share index tumbles 2.43 pct, nervous trade.

text.p: Blue-chips took a beating on Bombay bourses on Wednesday, with a shaky market undertone putting pressure on prices, traders said.
Poor results announced by major firms for the first-half of 1996/97 (April-March) undermined sentiment, as speculators took advantage and hammered prices, they said.
"Lack of participation from players and speculative selling in the market are pulling down share prices," said Vijay Bhatia, chief dealer at brokers Pashupati Advani.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) index crashed 76.22 points to a provisional 3,063.11 close, off 3,139.33, the day's high.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index fell 21.59 points, or 2.40 percent at a provisional close of 876.41.
Market participants said the onslaught of disappointing first half profit announcements this week had sent shaken investors and painted a gloomy market outlook.
"People are looking at the numbers and getting worried. In some cases, earnings are coming out even worse than expected," said Keshav Sanghi at James Capel B&K sales in Hong Kong.
Leading firms including Grasim Industries, Century Textiles and Hindalco Industries have announced a fall in net profits for the six-months ending September 30, 1996.
Dealers said rumours of an impending increase in petroleum prices also affected market sentiment. But, the Petroleum ministry said there were no plans now to raise oil prices.
"There is nothing afoot on increase in petroleum prices. It is not immediate," a ministry official who asked not to be named told Reuters on Wednesday.

Traders said foreign funds were sellers in TELCO, Gujarat Ambuja Cements, ITC and ACC. Reliance lost 8.0 rupees to 182.50, TISCO 7.50 rupees to 160.25, SBI 8.50 to 218.75, ACC 61.50 to 1,178.75 and ITC 6.75 to 273.75.
